Criptech:
A collective of disabled artists who use technologies, including assistive technologies, digital and scientific mediums, as an artistic medium and as a means of “crip practice.”
Crip technoscience: 
A field of scientific practice and knowledge of the political and technological systems that affect disabled people, or “crips”, reclaiming the term as a shared identity and not as a slur, where disabled people act as the “experts and designers of everyday life”, they work to change the systems that have and continue to oppress disabled people.
Praxis: From Ancient Greek, Lit practice by free people, the concept of putting a theory or practice into action. In the context of Crip Technoscience, this involves the knowledge, shared experiences and struggles of disabled people to provide a more just and accessible life.
title: Analysis of Criptech
introduction: For this weeks lesson, the class discussed the Access Riders that were submitted for this class, and then the class read along with the paper Criptech and the Art of Access: Introduction to Special Issue. After this lesson, I sat down to read the paper in more detail, make notes and ask questions about the terms that it uses.
